title: 2-deoxy-D-glucose CESL MRI of the rodent brain
author: Philipp Boehm-Sturm
materials: Goal: injected dose of 1 g/kg body weight.

Region of Interest (ROI) Analysis ROI analysis can be performed in two ways: ROI analyses. CESL images can be quantified in anatomical regions defined in the SIGMA rat brain atlas (a) or using manual delineation (b) of the lesion on ADC, CBF and late ΔR 1ρ maps (mean of the last 5 maps). Penumbra is defined via perfusion/diffusion mismatch. Figure reproduced from Boehm-Sturm et al., 2025 (doi: 10.1177/0271678X251355049 ) under a CC-BY-NC license.

Automatic analysis of brain regions of interest Segment brain regions automatically on the different MRI contrasts (T2, ADC, CBF, CESL) using a series of 3D to 3D and 3D to 2D image registrations using the SIGMA rat brain template (Barriere, et al., 2019). The registration can be performed for example in ANTx2 software (Koch, et al., 2019). ANTx2 all all https://github.com/ChariteExpMri/antx2 ChariteExpMRI Apply the registration to the SIGMA atlas, which matches the template. For registration, use the b = 0 image for diffusion MR images, the first inversion time image for perfusion MR images and the first TSL image for CESL images. For perfusion MRI, images will be distorted due to shimming artefacts of the EPI sequence and a nonlinear registration is needed. For ADC and CESL images, affine (12 degrees of freedom) registrations are sufficient.

steps.title: Anesthetize and prepare animal
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the rat with a 70 % N₂O / 30 % O₂ mixture, induce with 5 % isoflurane, maintain 1.75‑2.5 % isoflurane during femoral catheter implantation and the 90‑min MCAO surgery, then keep at 1.75 % isoflurane during MRI to obtain a respiration rate of ~60‑100 breaths/min. Implant a femoral catheter for later 2‑DG injection and perform a 90‑min middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) to induce focal cerebral ischemia.

steps.title: Prepare 2‑DG injection solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g 2‑deoxy‑D‑glucose (2‑DG) in ~3.3 mL sterile NaCl, then add NaCl to reach a final volume of 4 mL, giving a 25 % w/v solution (0.25 g mL⁻¹).

steps.title: Calculate injection volume
steps.instruction: Compute injection volume v = (dose × weight) / concentration = (1 g kg⁻¹ × body weight kg) / 0.25 g mL⁻¹ = 4 mL kg⁻¹. Example: a 400 g rat receives 1.6 mL (plus catheter dead volume).

steps.title: Acquire B0 map
steps.instruction: Create a B0 map with 3 averages, default field‑of‑view, and reconstruction S/N set to 20; then start the B0 mapping scan.

steps.title: Propagate slice orientation to T1ρ protocols
steps.instruction: Import the slice orientation defined in the WASABI scan into all subsequent T1ρ protocols (04_T1ρ_pre through 06_T1ρ_post).

steps.title: Inject 2‑DG during MRI
steps.instruction: Deliver the calculated 2‑DG solution slowly through the femoral catheter over 2 min, including the catheter dead volume.

steps.title: Perform in‑vivo CESL T1ρ MRI
steps.instruction: Execute the CESL MRI protocol excluding DWI and PWI; acquire a single T1ρ scan using a slice perpendicular to the NMR tubes as described in the T1ρ protocol section.

steps.title: Generate R1ρ maps
steps.instruction: Calculate voxel‑wise R1ρ (R1ρ = 1/T1ρ) by mono‑exponential fitting of signal intensities over the spin‑lock times (TSL) for each time point.

steps.title: Plot R1ρ versus 2‑DG concentration
steps.instruction: Plot the derived R1ρ values against the known 2‑DG concentrations of the phantom tubes and perform a linear regression; the resulting curve should resemble the published example.

steps.title: Extract ROI values and perform statistics
steps.instruction: Extract mean values from the defined regions of interest and conduct appropriate group statistical analyses matching the experimental design.
